featured.reason: Cloudflare's six-phase security-audit skill for coding agents: isolated hunters, adversarial verifiers, schema-validated findings.json and coverage ledger; needs a sub-agent-capable agent, Node.js for validators and an OS sandbox for any target builds.
ideas: Install it with `npx skills add ... --skill security-audit` and run "security audit this codebase" on one of your own web apps, then read the REPORT.md and NEEDS-VALIDATION.md it derives.
Point it at an Android app repo you own and let it use DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md to hunt deep-link, webview and exported-component issues.
Study how it keeps the finder and the verifier as separate agents, and reuse that disprove-first pattern in your own multi-agent workflows.
Run it twice on the same repo and compare coverage-ledger.json between runs to see what the additive second pass adds (the authors report roughly half the findings come from repeat runs).
Learn report-schema.json and the zero-dependency validate-findings.cjs, and adapt the schema-validated findings idea for code-review or QA outputs from your agents.

featured.reason: /graphify skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 20+ assistants that turns a repo plus docs/PDFs into a local tree-sitter knowledge graph (graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json) agents query instead of grepping; doc/media pass uses your model; Graphify Cloud is an optional paid upsell.
ideas: Run `/graphify .` on ai-daily-radar or a client repo and open graph.html to see god nodes and detected subsystems before you start a refactor.
Use `graphify path` and `graphify explain` on an unfamiliar codebase (for example a large open-source app) to trace how two components connect without reading every file.
Add `# WHY:` / `# NOTE:` comments and ADR files to a project and see them become linked rationale nodes that agents can query.
Feed a folder of PDFs or design docs alongside the code to build one graph that links specs to implementation (the doc pass uses your assistant's model).
Compare token use for the same codebase question with and without querying graph.json, to judge whether a graph beats grep for your projects.

featured.reason: One-prompt skill/plugin for Claude Code, Codex and ~20 agents that pushes minimal, reuse-first code without cutting validation, security or tests, plus /ponytail-review, -audit and -debt commands; Codex install asks you to trust two lifecycle hooks.
ideas: Install it as a Claude Code plugin (/plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail) and give the same small feature to the agent with ponytail on and off, then compare diff size and tests.
Run /ponytail-review on your next pull request to get a review that reads the touched code, checks security and load, and flags risky logic without a test.
Run /ponytail-audit on an older project to get a ranked fix-first list of bugs, slow paths and code to cut.
Use /ponytail-debt to collect the `shortcut:` comments agents leave behind into a ledger you actually revisit.
Read its single SKILL.md and AGENTS.md to learn how one compact prompt changes agent behavior, then borrow the reuse-first ladder for your own rules files.
